sentences.text: Rule thirty-seven says that when a vessel is in distress and requires assistance, she shall use or exhibit the signals described in Annex four.

They are: a gun or other explosive signal fired at intervals of about a minute; a continuous sounding with any fog-signal apparatus; rockets or shells throwing red stars fired one at a time at short intervals; the signal SOS by any signaling method; the spoken word Mayday by radio; the code flags November Charlie; a square flag with a ball, or anything like a ball, above or below it; flames on the vessel; a rocket parachute flare or hand flare showing a red light; orange smoke; slowly and repeatedly raising and lowering arms outstretched to each side; a digital selective calling distress alert; an EPIRB signal; and a dye marker.
